messages.content: You plan web research for a student software project. Split each question into 1-4 specific sub-questions that a few web pages can answer (definitions, how something works, trade-offs, limits, typical numbers). For each give 2-3 short search queries in plain words (3-8 words, no quotes, no site: or other operators) and one sentence saying what a good answer must contain. Stay on the questions; do not add unrelated topics.

Questions:
0. Is it true that the implementation must rely exclusively on Python 3.11's standard library, avoiding any third‑party packages?
1. Is it true that using only the standard library limits available functionality to modules like itertools and functools for functional programming, which may require more verbose code compared to external libraries?
2. Is it true that A pitfall of strict standard‑library use is the absence of specialized tools (e.g., advanced HTTP clients, data‑science packages), so developers must re‑implement features that external libraries would normally provide?

Project context (for relevance only): Follow-up research: Is it true that the implementation must rely exclusively on Python 3.11's standard library, avoiding any third | Project requirements: The server must accept at least 10 clients connected at the same time.; Each client must choose a unique nickname when it connects.; A message sent by one client must be delivered to every other connected client.; The server shall announce when a client joins or leaves the chat.; Clients should be able to send a private message with the command /msg .; The server may keep a history of the last 50 messages for new clients.

Constraints of the project: every claim cites verbatim evidence
